• Full-stack delivery. Design, build and scale backend services in Go and product experiences in TypeScript and React. Turn large volumes of cost and usage data into interfaces that make the answer obvious - clear, fast and trustworthy enough to base financial decisions on.

• API-first. Build capabilities so they're fully available through APIs, not just the UI. Both humans and agents should be able to drive the platform.

Ready to revolutionize healthcare, making it faster and more accessible than ever before? 

How we started:

Founded in 2013 by Dwayne D’Souza, HeliosX   was built on a simple but powerful idea: healthcare should be easier to access, faster to receive, and centred around the individual. From day one, we’ve grown without external funding; scaling profitably through technology, disciplined execution, and deep medical expertise. What started as a challenger idea has become one of the most significant healthcare platforms operating globally today.

Where we are now:

We’ve earned the trust of millions of people worldwide through category-leading products and well-known brands, including MedExpress, Dermatica, ZipHealth, RocketRX, and Levity. A key driver of our success is vertical integration; we operate our own manufacturing and proprietary products, led by in-house medical teams, researchers, and pharmacists at the top of their fields.

In 2025, HeliosX treated more than 1.7 million patients globally and reached £781m in revenue, representing +337% year-on-year growth and cementing our position as the clear market leader in the UK. That growth translates into real-world outcomes: our weight-loss treatments helped patients lose 8.5 million kilograms of excess weight in 2025 alone, contributing to an estimated 1,300 fewer cardiac events. This is growth with measurable, life-changing impact at scale.

Today, we operate across four international markets, with successful launches in Germany and Canada and continued expansion in the US. We were also recently recognised in the Sunday Times Top 100 fastest-growing tech companies, further validation of both our momentum and our ambition.

Where we’re going:

2026 is another significant year for HeliosX. Our ambition is to surpass £1.1bn in revenue, continue expanding thoughtfully into new international markets and broaden our condition and treatment portfolio. As we scale, we're focused on building the technology, operational excellence and clinical capabilities that will support sustainable long-term growth. Joining HeliosX now means helping shape the systems, teams and products that will define the next chapter of digital healthcare. You'll be solving complex problems at pace, working alongside exceptional people and building products that genuinely improve lives at scale.

There’s never been a more exciting time to join HeliosX. Come be a part of making our dream of easier and faster healthcare a reality!

You will lead clinical audits, risk management assessments & safety error-reporting frameworks, as well as playing a central role in quality assurance, policy development & regulatory compliance across the pharmacy function.

You will need to be pragmatic & solution-focused, comfortable working at pace & able to represent HeliosX credibly with external professional bodies and stakeholders.

HELLO!

I'm Allie, Head of Support at Ashby. 👋 Support at Ashby is a strategic differentiator. As we've scaled, we've built out dedicated functions to support it: a Systems Engineer keeping our tooling running, a Workforce Management practice ensuring we have the right coverage at the right times, a Quality program that keeps every interaction excellent, and a Training function that gets new hires up to speed fast. Each of these functions is strong on its own. What we're missing is someone to bring them together. That's why we're hiring our first Senior Support Operations Manager to lead the Support Operations organization: Systems, Workforce Management, Quality, and Training. You'll report directly to me.

This role isn't about running any one of these functions day to day. It's about setting the systems, processes, and standards that let them work together, coaching and developing the leaders who own them, and ensuring the systems and processes behind Support match the customer experience we want to deliver. You won't own the hands-on systems administration, forecasting, quality evaluations, or training delivery, but you'll be expected to understand that work well enough to ask sharp questions, spot patterns across functions, and have real problem-solving conversations with the leads who own it day to day. You'll also be a key partner to our Knowledge Management team, helping turn what we know into self-service and in-app experiences that reduce the need for a ticket in the first place.

If you love building operational rigor while creating an environment where team members are eager to grow, staying close enough to the work to coach from firsthand understanding, and treating efficiency and quality as two sides of the same coin, this might be the role for you.

Our team will be at our company offsite from October 5-9. Applications will remain open during that time, and we’ll begin reviewing them the week of October 12.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As the Senior Support Operations Manager, you'll own the strategy, standards, and coordination across Ashby's Support Operations functions. You'll manage through the leaders who own each function's day-to-day execution, but you'll stay close to the work by regularly reviewing QA scores, joining forecasting reviews, and understanding systems changes well enough that your coaching is specific, not just directional. Because this is a new layer of leadership and Support Operations is still being established, you'll have the authority to define how these functions coordinate, where they should be more tightly integrated, and where efficiency gains can free up capacity for higher-impact work. In your first year, you'll establish consistent processes and standards across the four functions, formalize how the functions work together, and help drive measurable improvements in efficiency or quality.

Integrating Systems, WFM, Quality, and Training

- Manage and coordinate Support Operations' four functions: Systems, Workforce Management, Quality, and Training, ensuring they operate as a cohesive organization supporting our Specialists and Support Engineers.

- Plan and implement operational policies, standards, and recurring practices that bring consistency across functions while respecting what makes each one distinct.

- Identify where functions should work more closely together (e.g., how Quality findings inform Training content, or how WFM forecasts should account for Systems changes) and drive that integration.

Managing and Developing the Leaders of Each Function

- Directly manage the leaders and individual contributors across Systems, Workforce Management, Quality, and Training, including several who are new to their roles and still establishing their own operating standards.

- Coach and develop the leaders of each function as they grow their programs, hire their teams, and establish operating standards, grounding that coaching in specific, detailed feedback.
